question: At what roof age does Ostermere normally request a roof inspection at underwriting?
key_points: More than 20 years generally (INS-SYN-003); more than 15 years only for new business in zone H3 (INS-SYN-004, from 2026-03-01)
notes: Trap 1, scoped supersession: 15 years reported as the general rule is wrong. The checks need both figures and the scope; a person should confirm 15 is not presented as universal.

question: Does the 15-year roof inspection threshold apply to policies that were already in force before the zone model?

documents: Re: Roof threshold for the new severe-wind zone

key_points: No: new business in zone H3 only; not retro-fitted to in-force policies (INS-SYN-004; Vasquez email, INS-SYN-018)

question: Is trace and access covered under Hearthmere?

documents: Claims Handling Manual - Chapter 7 - Water Damage

key_points: Unresolved conflict (con-001): the Claims Handling Manual (INS-SYN-012) says covered as standard up to EUR 5,000; the Endorsement Catalogue (INS-SYN-008) says optional paid endorsement HS-TA-01 (EUR 5,000, EUR 24 premium). Both current. A correct answer presents both and does not pick one.
notes: Trap 2, the load-bearing one. Picking either side fails the facts check. Also grade by hand: does it avoid choosing?

question: Who is responsible for resolving the trace-and-access question, and what should claim handlers do until then?
key_points: Y. Tanaka (Product) is the accountable owner; handlers refer all trace-and-access questions and quote no figure (minutes of 2026-05-06)

question: Are cash settlement basis, actual cash value, depreciated value, ACV, depreciation holdback and recoverable depreciation six different things?

documents: RE: Hearthmere - clarification on cash settlement basis

key_points: No, two things: cash settlement basis = actual cash value = depreciated value = ACV; depreciation holdback = recoverable depreciation (Broker Support reply, 2026-03-11)

question: For claim CLM-1108, did the 15-year H3 roof inspection threshold apply?
key_points: No: the loss was on 2026-02-20 and the H3 rule took effect on 2026-03-01 (and applies to new business; the policy was written 2025-09-14). The general 20-year rule applied, and the roof (about 17 at underwriting) was below it.

question: A Hearthmere building loss happened on 1 August 2025. Is depreciation recoverable on that claim?

documents: RE: Hearthmere - clarification on cash settlement basis

key_points: No: v1.1 (in force to 2025-12-31) governs that loss, settling on ACV with depreciation not recoverable; v1.2 introduced recoverable depreciation from 2026-01-01
notes: Trap 4 in reverse: the superseded version is the right one for an older loss.

question: Why is the H3 roof inspection threshold 15 years rather than 20?

documents: Re: Roof threshold for the new severe-wind zone

key_points: Between 15 and 20 years, covering displacement in the severe-wind band is about 3.4x the standard band at the same age (E. Vasquez email, 2026-01-22); below 15 the bands are similar
notes: Trap 5, rationale that lives only in an email.

question: Why was CLM-1042 triaged at Level 1?
key_points: Property habitable, water source stopped, estimate EUR 3,800, below the EUR 5,000 Level 1 limit (claim notes INS-SYN-005; triage guideline INS-SYN-002)

question: Why might CLM-1155 fall outside escape-of-water cover when CLM-1042 did not?
key_points: CLM-1155 shows continuous or repeated seepage (excluded under 4.2); CLM-1042 was a datable, sudden connector failure. CLM-1155's position is provisional; declining needs a claims professional.

question: Can the AI assistant assign a triage level or approve coverage on a claim?
key_points: It may suggest a provisional triage level; it must not approve or deny coverage, determine fraud or replace emergency instructions (INS-SYN-002)

question: Who did E. Vasquez email about the roof threshold, and when?
key_points: D. Lindqvist (cc M. Oyelaran), 2026-01-22; Lindqvist replied the same day
notes: The only graph question: the corpus has names but no email addresses.

question: How many in-force Hearthmere policies carry the HS-TA-01 endorsement?
key_points: Not known yet: establishing it is Y. Tanaka's open action (due 2026-05-20). Any number is invented.
notes: The count is in no source. A good answer says so and points to the open action; a person should check that no number was invented.

question: What is the policy excess on a Hearthmere escape-of-water claim?
key_points: Not in the sources: no document states an excess or deductible.
notes: The strict check fails an answer that cites anything; read those by hand.
